metadata.title: Robot Wiki
metadata.description: Citation-first encyclopedia of modern robot learning.

metadata.title: A-Z Index
metadata.description: Every published Robot Wiki article and glossary term in one alphabetical list.

metadata.title: About Robot Wiki: Scope and Reading Order
metadata.description: About Robot Wiki: what it covers and excludes, the order to read its articles in, what they assume you know and how its citations work.

metadata.title: Adjacent Domains
metadata.description: Adjacent domains are robotics fields that meet the same problems under their own safety and certification rules: driving, drones, surgery and space.

metadata.title: Autonomous Vehicles
metadata.description: Driving as a robotics problem, down to the long tail.

metadata.title: Drones and Aerial Robotics
metadata.description: Autonomous flight, from state estimation to champion-level racing.

metadata.title: Space Robotics
metadata.description: Robots where repair is impossible, from Mars to orbit.

metadata.title: Surgical Robotics
metadata.description: From da Vinci to Hugo and OTTAVA, authorized one indication at a time.

metadata.title: Classical Foundations
metadata.description: Classical robotics is the model-based stack that learned policies still run on: kinematics, planning, control, estimation, grasping, perception, mapping, calibration and ROS 2.

metadata.title: Robot Calibration
metadata.description: The measurements that make sensor coordinates agree with motion.

metadata.title: Control
metadata.description: PID, LQR, MPC and whole-body QP, the stack under every learned policy.

metadata.title: Grasp Planning
metadata.description: Contact mechanics, grasp quality metrics, and force closure.

metadata.title: Kinematics
metadata.description: How joint angles place a robot's hand, and the reverse.

metadata.title: Motion Planning
metadata.description: Configuration space, RRT and its variants, and trajectory optimization.

metadata.title: Perception for Manipulation
metadata.description: How camera images become an object's position and orientation.

metadata.title: ROS 2 for Machine Learning Engineers
metadata.description: ROS 2 as the production boundary around a learned policy.

metadata.title: Scene Representation and Mapping
metadata.description: From point clouds to Gaussian splats: what a robot remembers about space.

metadata.title: State Estimation
metadata.description: Kalman filters, factor graphs, and pose estimation from noisy sensors.

metadata.title: Credits
metadata.description: Every photograph and diagram on Robot Wiki, with its creator, source, and licence.

metadata.title: Data, Hardware & Evaluation
metadata.description: Data, hardware and evaluation are what robot learning runs on: training data, the robots that collect it and the tests that score results.

metadata.title: The Data Bottleneck
metadata.description: Robot data comes in hours; language data in trillions of tokens.

metadata.title: Major Datasets
metadata.description: The major open robot datasets and what each collected.

metadata.title: The Evaluation Crisis
metadata.description: What a success rate hides, from trial count to scorer.

metadata.title: Hardware Taxonomy
metadata.description: A buyer's guide from SO-101 to Jetson Thor.

metadata.title: Industrial Deployment
metadata.description: The jam-rate arithmetic that decides whether a 99 percent cell ships.

metadata.title: The Robot Learning Stack
metadata.description: From data capture to robot integration as one reproducible system.

metadata.title: Teleoperation Rigs
metadata.description: ALOHA, GELLO, UMI and VR rigs compared on cost and quality.

metadata.title: Editorial Policy: Sources, Review, Corrections
metadata.description: Robot Wiki's editorial policy: how its robotics articles are researched, cited, reviewed, corrected and updated, plus how to report an error.

metadata.title: Frontier & Open Problems
metadata.description: Frontier problems are the open questions that keep robot demos from becoming products: reliability, dexterity, generalization and safety.

metadata.title: The Bear Case
metadata.description: Why this could be another robotics winter.

metadata.title: Competing Theses
metadata.description: Six bets on how robot intelligence gets built.

metadata.title: Dexterity
metadata.description: Contact-rich manipulation, touch sensing, in-hand reorientation and deformables.

metadata.title: Generalization
metadata.description: From pi0.5's three unseen homes to Helix 2.5's 30.

metadata.title: The Reliability Gap
metadata.description: 80% task success is a demo; 99.9% is a product.

metadata.title: Safety and Assurance
metadata.description: What ships is a verifiable safety layer around the learned policy.

metadata.title: Glossary
metadata.description: Cited definitions of the robotics and machine-learning terms used across Robot Wiki.

metadata.title: How Robots Work: Interactive 3D Explainers
metadata.description: How robots work, in interactive 3D explainers: guess first, then drag, push or tilt a robot model to see why, with a source for every number.

metadata.title: Manipulation & Learned Policies
metadata.description: Manipulation is a robot handling objects with its arms and hands, and a learned policy maps what the robot senses to its next action.

metadata.title: Action Chunking (ACT and ALOHA)
metadata.description: ACT predicts short action sequences and smooths them with temporal ensembling.

metadata.title: Action Spaces for Robot Learning
metadata.description: What each action representation gives the learner and asks of the controller.

metadata.title: Behavior Cloning Foundations
metadata.description: Covariate shift makes naive imitation drift, and DAgger is the standard fix.

metadata.title: Comparison Matrix
metadata.description: Every major policy compared on eight architectural axes.

metadata.title: Cross-Embodiment Transfer
metadata.description: How one policy learns from many robot bodies and from humans.

metadata.title: Diffusion Policy
metadata.description: Visuomotor control as conditional denoising over action sequences, with receding-horizon execution.

metadata.title: Foundation Models for Robotics
metadata.description: What foundation means in robotics, and what adaptation still costs.

metadata.title: Other Generalist Policies
metadata.description: How to read the claims for Gemini Robotics, GR00T, Helix and GO-2.

metadata.title: Hierarchical Approaches
metadata.description: From SayCan and Code as Policies to the hierarchies in Helix and pi0.5.

metadata.title: Knowledge Insulation
metadata.description: Discrete tokens train the backbone while the action expert trains behind a stop-gradient.

metadata.title: The Pi Line
metadata.description: From pi0 to pi0.7, with flow-matching action experts and FAST tokenization.

metadata.title: Real-Time Execution
metadata.description: The latency budgets that decide whether the control loop closes.

metadata.title: RL Fine-Tuning of Policies
metadata.description: Improving a pretrained policy from its own online experience.

metadata.title: Robot Learning Curriculum for ML Engineers
metadata.description: A dependency-ordered route from supervised learning to real robot policies.

metadata.title: Vision-Language-Action Models
metadata.description: RT-1, RT-2, Octo and OpenVLA, and what web-scale pretraining adds to robot control.

metadata.title: Market Map
metadata.description: The embodied-AI industry as data: companies across six segments, filterable by approach, geography, stage, and funding.

metadata.title: 3D Kinematics Playground
metadata.description: A SO-101 robot arm rendered from its URDF in the browser: joint sliders for forward kinematics, click-to-reach inverse kinematics, and trajectory record/replay.

metadata.title: Privacy and Anonymous Analytics
metadata.description: Privacy on Robot Wiki: what anonymous traffic information it measures, why it is collected and what is deliberately excluded.

metadata.title: RL, Sim-to-Real & Locomotion
metadata.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) is trial-and-error training of a robot controller, usually in simulation before transfer to hardware.

metadata.title: Humanoid Whole-Body Control
metadata.description: How humanoids track retargeted human motion.

metadata.title: Legged Locomotion Lineage
metadata.description: How learned gaits became the default for legged robots.

metadata.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Robotics
metadata.description: CQL and TD3+BC, and when behavior cloning is the stronger baseline.

metadata.title: Massively Parallel Sim RL
metadata.description: GPU-parallel simulation with Isaac Lab, Newton, MJX and Brax.

metadata.title: Reward Design and the MPC Debate
metadata.description: Hand-tuned and language-model rewards, and the MPC debate.

metadata.title: RL for Robotics
metadata.description: Sample efficiency decides which RL algorithm a robot can use.

metadata.title: Sim-to-Real Transfer
metadata.description: Domain randomization, distillation, system identification and real-to-sim reconstruction.

metadata.title: Why RL Won Locomotion but Not Manipulation
metadata.description: Walking is cheap to simulate; contact-rich manipulation is not.

metadata.title: Search
metadata.description: Search Robot Wiki: full-text over article prose plus the structured data layer (methods, companies, datasets).

metadata.title: World Models
metadata.description: World models are learned models that predict how an environment changes when a robot acts, so it can plan, train or be tested on predictions. World-action models also predict actions and run as policies.

metadata.title: World Model Evaluation for Robotics
metadata.description: Testing a world model on what a robot needs.

metadata.title: Generative Simulation
metadata.description: Generated tasks, scenes and assets inside a physics engine.

metadata.title: Generative Video World Models
metadata.description: Cosmos, Genie and GR-2 use action-conditioned video prediction as a simulator.

metadata.title: JEPA and the Non-Generative Counterargument
metadata.description: V-JEPA 2 and 2.1 predict in representation space, with no pixel decoder.

metadata.title: Latent-Dynamics World Models
metadata.description: Dreamer 4, TD-MPC2 and Newt: compact learned dynamics for imagination-based control.

metadata.title: Model-Based Robot Learning
metadata.description: Learn dynamics, plan through them, and improve from imagined rollouts.

metadata.title: What Is a World Model?
metadata.description: Six example groups compared, from DreamerV3 to V-JEPA 2.

metadata.title: World Models vs Physics Simulators
metadata.description: Learned dynamics, physics engines and hybrids compared as robot simulators.
